summary: The Flame in Freefall project tackles the critical challenge of spacecraft fire safety by applying Synthetic Intelligence (SI) to decades of NASA microgravity combustion data. In space, the absence of gravity-driven convection transforms familiar teardrop flames into quiet, spherical burns that behave unpredictably, especially in the high-oxygen, low-pressure environments planned for future Moon and Mars habitats. Because astronauts cannot evacuate during an emergency and the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database holds terabytes of complex experimental results, engineers need a faster way to extract actionable safety insights. This project proposes an interactive, SI-powered dashboard that analyzes, summarizes, and ranks key datasets—covering solid flammability, smoke detection, and flame suppression—to help mission designers choose safer cabin materials, optimize fire-suppression systems, and improve firefighting technology on Earth.
details: Our conceptual dashboard uses no-code AI workflows, data visualization tools, and presentation software to synthesize and rank NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data. Built around mission-critical factors like low pressure, high oxygen levels, and restricted crew evacuation, our solution creatively bridges complex space physics with an intuitive visual risk guide and interactive user mockups. This empowers aerospace engineers to rapidly select fire-resistant materials and design superior smoke detection and suppression systems, ultimately protecting astronauts on future Moon and Mars missions while inspiring safer firefighting technologies back on Earth.
